channel.title: Kurs Media
channel.description: Russian business conflicts, money and power: what happened, what it costs and who benefits.

item.title: Banks v. telecom operators: Russia's fight over who pays for the networks
item.description: Russia's four big mobile operators and its largest banks are locked in a dispute over money. First came fees for labelling banks' calls; now the Digital Development Ministry is drafting restrictions on virtual operators, many of them bank-owned. The parties, the numbers and what comes next.

item.title: Shelf price vs. register price: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General over overcharges
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission and 20 states have sued Dollar General, alleging that the 21,000-store discount chain charged shoppers more at the register than its shelf prices for years. The company has paid six states $6 million over similar claims since 2019.

item.title: Sanctions with interest: Rusal seeks $1.3 billion from Rio Tinto and takes aim at Mongolian copper
item.description: A Russian court has ordered Rio Tinto to pay Rusal $1.278 billion over its exclusion from an Australian alumina refinery and has levied execution on Rio's 66% stake in the operator of Mongolia's Oyu Tolgoi copper mine. The parties' positions and what comes next.

item.title: Rusnano v. Chubais: bailiffs pursue nearly 20 billion rubles over a failed school tablet and MRAM chips
item.description: Russia's Federal Bailiff Service has opened 14 enforcement proceedings against former Rusnano chief Anatoly Chubais worth nearly 20 billion rubles (about $240 million). They stem from Moscow Arbitration Court rulings on losses from the Plastic Logic and Crocus projects.
